title: Integrate capacity headroom signal into routing decisions (staged rollout)
author: Ravi Menon
release_notes: Adds an optional routing signal sourced from fleet headroom to reduce overload during regional impairments; gated by feature flag and defaults to no-op.
description: Motivation: During regional impairments we’ve seen failover triggers succeed but the destination region overloads due to insufficient GPU headroom, which amplifies tail latency and 5xx spikes (thundering herd + retries). This PR wires a first-class capacity/headroom signal into routing/policy evaluation so routing can proactively degrade/fail over (or shed) before we run regions into saturation. Summary of changes: (1) Adds a Fleet Capacity client that exposes per-region headroom for Hosted pools and Dedicated pools (aggregate + per-pool guardrails) with caching and jitter to avoid stampedes. (2) Extends the routing policy engine with a new predicate `capacity_ok(region, route)` and a numeric signal `capacity_headroom_pct` that can be used in deterministic signal hierarchy rules (coexists with reachability / 5xx burn / latency burn). (3) Introduces thresholds + hold-down semantics: headroom is considered unhealthy when `headroom_pct < min_headroom_pct` OR `queue_depth > max_queue_depth` for N consecutive windows; recovery requires `headroom_pct > min_headroom_pct + hysteresis_pct` for M windows; all parameters are config-driven and default to safe/no-op. (4) Adds staged rollout flag `routing.capacity_signal.enabled` with per-tier and per-tenant allowlist support; initial recommended rollout is Hosted API only, dry-run mode emitting audit events and dashboards, then enforce. (5) Observability: emits `routing_capacity_gate_total{decision=allow|deny, reason=low_headroom|queue_depth, region, route_class}` and traces include capacity snapshot used for the decision; adds debug logging behind `ROUTING_CAPACITY_DEBUG=1` for on-call triage. Testing: unit tests cover thresholding/hysteresis, missing data behavior (fails open by default), and determinism; integration tests stub fleet service and validate no extra routing latency under load. Rollout plan: enable in staging with dry-run for 48h; verify dashboard alignment with existing latency/5xx burn panels; then production enable for internal tenants + a small Hosted allowlist; Dedicated enforcement remains disabled until drain automation is in place (ENG-2420).
commits: routing: add capacity signal interface + wiring into policy evaluation
fleet: implement headroom client (cache + jitter) and basic region aggregation
policy-engine: add capacity_ok predicate + config schema + determinism tests
routing: add feature flag + allowlist + dry-run audit event emission
observability: add routing_capacity_gate metrics + trace attributes
docs: add operator notes for tuning thresholds and reading dashboards
review_conversation: Mina Haddad (review): Can we confirm behavior when fleet-capacity is missing/slow? We should avoid blocking routing on an auxiliary dependency during partial outages. Also please clarify whether a capacity deny results in failover vs local shed.

Ravi Menon (author): Updated to fail-open by default (`capacity_signal.mode=observe|enforce`, default observe; enforce uses fail-open on missing/expired data with metric `reason=missing_data`). Decision pipeline now distinguishes (a) "deny -> try next region" vs (b) "deny -> shed" depending on route class and retry budget; documented in the internal doc and added tests.

Vanessa Ortiz (review): Thresholds: min_headroom_pct=15% seems low for bursty token workloads, and we should include hysteresis to prevent flapping. Also: are we using queue depth that’s comparable across models/pools?

Ravi Menon (author): Added `hysteresis_pct` and separate consecutive-window requirements for degrade/recover. Defaults set conservatively: min_headroom_pct=25, hysteresis=10, consecutive_unhealthy=3, consecutive_healthy=6 (all config). Queue depth is normalized by pool capacity (`queue_depth_per_gpu`) for Hosted; for Dedicated we only publish aggregate "can_accept" until pool drain automation lands (ENG-2420).

Keiko Yamamoto (review): Feature flag scoping: please ensure we can enable by tenant tier and allowlist specific tenants; we also need a rate limit on policy flips when this starts influencing routing.

Ravi Menon (author): Added tier-based gate + explicit allowlist and wired into existing `policy_flip_rate_limit` (this signal only affects candidate regions; it doesn’t directly flip policies, but it can drive a failover decision; added audit events for "capacity_gate_triggered" so we can correlate).

Miles Thornton (review): Interaction with failover trigger hierarchy: capacity should not override reachability, but it should block routing into a region that is reachable yet saturated. Can we make the evaluation deterministic and visible in logs?

Ravi Menon (author): Capacity is treated as a gating signal in the region scoring stage (post reachability check, pre final selection). Policy evaluation remains deterministic (inputs are the cached snapshot + request metadata). Added structured log `routing_decision.capacity_snapshot` with region->(headroom_pct, queue_norm, ts) behind debug flag and trace attributes always-on.

Allison Grant (review): Metrics labels: please keep route labels low-cardinality; prefer route_class or service rather than raw route. Also add a dashboard note about expected changes during game days.

Ravi Menon (author): Adjusted metric labels to `route_class` (hosted_chat|hosted_embeddings|dedicated) and `region`. Added doc section "How to read capacity gate metrics during failover" and confirmed no tenant_id labels. (Follow-up on broader metric cardinality is tracked separately.)
Mina Haddad (approval): Looks good after updates; please ensure staging config defaults to observe-only.
Vanessa Ortiz (approval): Approved; will help tune thresholds after 24h staging data.
Keiko Yamamoto (approval): Approved with rollout gating in place.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash into main by Mina Haddad. Post-merge note: staged rollout flag remains disabled in production by default; enablement will be driven by ENG-2414 rollout checklist.
